name: Lana Del Rey
label: Interscope / Polydor
lede: She was Lizzy Grant, then May Jailer, then a record pulled from iTunes by its own label, and then a webcam video that started a career. Her ninth album landed at No. 11 on Pitchfork's 2023 list.

eras.title: Lizzy Grant, before the name
eras.text: A Manhattan-born Fordham philosophy student records under other names, signs a small deal, makes a full album, and watches the label pull it. Almost nobody hears any of it, which is the point of the next chapter.

years.h: Sirens: an acoustic album as May Jailer
years.p: Before Lana Del Rey, Elizabeth Woolridge Grant recorded an acoustic album called Sirens under the name May Jailer.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia, she was born in Manhattan on June 21, 1985, and later earned a philosophy degree at Fordham University (2008). Sirens is the earliest recording in her catalog and stayed off the market.

years.h: Kill Kill EP, credited to Lizzy Grant
years.p: The name on the cover was Lizzy Grant, before the Lana Del Rey name existed.
years.xp: The self-titled 2010 album's cover would later carry the line "Lana Del Ray A.K.A. Lizzy Grant", which nods to the Kill Kill EP name she used in 2008, according to Wikipedia.

years.src: Wikipedia: Lana Del Ray (album) · Wikipedia: Lana Del Rey
years.h: Lana Del Ray: 13 tracks, out on iTunes for a few months
years.p: Producer David Kahne recorded it with her over three months in 2008. The spelling was Ray, after actress Lana Turner and the Ford Del Rey sedan.
years.xp:
5 Points Records released it through iTunes and Amazon MP3, then pulled it within three months of an April 1, 2010 separation agreement. Del Rey has said the label "was unable to fund it", per Wikipedia.

After Born to Die, she said in January 2012 she would re-release it once she owned the rights. That never happened. Only "Yayo" was officially reworked, on the 2012 Paradise EP, and the album exists now as bootlegs and digital archives.

years.h: She meets managers Ben Mawson and Ed Millett and moves to London
years.p: The pair took her on after the 5 Points deal fell apart, and London became the base for what came next.

eras.title: A webcam, a YouTube upload, and a lot of noise
eras.text: One self-made video sets the whole machine going. Then an SNL performance turns the backlash into a national argument, and Born to Die sells anyway.

years.cap: Lana Del Rey - Primavera Sound, Barcelona - Friday 31st May 2024 · Wikimedia
years.src: Wikipedia: Video Games (Lana Del Rey song) · Wikipedia: Born to Die (album)
years.h: Video Games goes online, and she made the video herself
years.p: She edited webcam footage of herself together with archive clips and paparazzi footage. Justin Parker co-wrote the song; Robopop produced it at BMG Studios in New York.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia, she put the song out with no plan to promote it as a single. It went viral on YouTube, was picked up for The CW's Ringer in September 2011, and came out through Stranger Records that June.

Interscope and Polydor signed her that November, and the song was re-released on October 7, 2011 as the lead single from Born to Die. Pitchfork named it Best New Music. It won the 2012 Ivor Novello for Best Contemporary Song.

years.h: Q Award for "Next Big Thing", weeks before the Interscope deal
years.p: The Q trophy arrived in October 2011. The joint Interscope and Polydor signing followed in November.

q: never had a persona. Never needed one. Never will.
years.src: Wikipedia: Born to Die (album) · Wikipedia: Lana Del Rey · Consequence: Lana Del Rey Headlines Coachella
years.h: Saturday Night Live, and the reviews that followed
years.p: NBC anchor Brian Williams used those words about her performance of "Video Games" and "Blue Jeans". Cast member Andy Samberg and host Daniel Radcliffe defended her.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia, Samberg and Radcliffe put the negativity down to her past and her family, not the performance itself. In 2024 she brought the moment back on purpose: her Coachella set included a hologram performance she framed as a callback to SNL.

years.h: Born to Die goes to No. 2 and sells 3.4 million in 2012
years.p: Emile Haynie, Rick Nowels and Robopop produced most of it, across studios from London to Electric Lady.
years.xp:
Wikipedia lists it as the world's fifth best-selling album of 2012. Pitchfork's first score was 5.5; the site rescored it more warmly in 2021, calling it "thrillingly rich", per Wikipedia. Metacritic has it at 62 from 37 reviews.

By December 2025 it had spent 618 weeks on the Billboard 200, the longest run by a female artist, according to Wikipedia.

years.src: Wikipedia: Lana Del Rey · Wikipedia: Lana Del Ray (album)
years.h: Paradise EP debuts at No. 10 on the Billboard 200
years.p: It carried "Yayo", reworked from the shelved 2010 album, and the Born to Die tracks in one package.

eras.title: From Cinerama Dome to Nashville
eras.text: A remix makes her a radio star, a short film reintroduces her as an auteur, and Dan Auerbach turns the sound to guitars. Honeymoon then goes back to strings.

years.h: A rejected Cedric Gervais remix takes "Summertime Sadness" to No. 6
years.p: Her label passed on the remix at first. It went to No. 1 on Beatport, then on to BBC Radio 1 and the Billboard Hot 100.
years.xp: The original came out June 22, 2012, produced by Emile Haynie and Rick Nowels. Gervais's version became her highest-charting US single at No. 6 and won the 2014 Grammy for Best Remixed Recording, Non-Classical, according to Wikipedia.

years.cap: Lana Del Rey performing live at the Grammy Museum in Los Angeles on 10/13/2019. · Wikimedia
years.src: Wikipedia: Lana Del Rey · Wikipedia: Ultraviolence (album) · Wikipedia: Lana Del Rey videography
years.h: Tropico premieres at the Cinerama Dome, and she names her next album there
years.p: Anthony Mandler directed the short film she wrote and starred in. She used the night to announce the title Ultraviolence.
years.xp: The title comes from Anthony Burgess's novella A Clockwork Orange, per Wikipedia. Earlier in 2013 she had also released "Young and Beautiful" for The Great Gatsby soundtrack.

years.cap: Ultraviolence, recorded with Dan Auerbach in Nashville
years.h: Ultraviolence: three days with Dan Auerbach become six weeks
years.p: The Black Keys' Auerbach recorded her live at his Easy Eye Sound studio in Nashville.
years.xp: It opened at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 and topped charts in 12 countries. Auerbach said every criticism he had heard about her was proven wrong in the studio, per Wikipedia. Pitchfork scored it 7.1; Metacritic 74.

years.h: Honeymoon enters at No. 2, with a cover shot by her sister
years.p: Chuck Grant photographed her on a Los Angeles Starline tour bus after a session with Neil Krug felt off.
years.xp: Rick Nowels and Kieron Menzies produced it in Santa Monica and New York. It sold 116,000 units in its first US week, per Wikipedia. Pitchfork gave it 7.5 and Metacritic 78.

eras.title: The poppier turn, then the peak
eras.text: Lust for Life brings guests and daylight. Then Norman Fucking Rockwell! with Jack Antonoff lands her the Album of the Year nomination and the top critic ranking of 2019.

years.src: Wikipedia: Lust for Life (Lana Del Rey album)
years.h: Lust for Life: The Weeknd, A$AP Rocky and Stevie Nicks
years.p: Playboi Carti and Sean Ono Lennon also appear on a No. 1 debut in the US and UK.
years.xp: Pitchfork gave it 7.7 and said it presented the "sad girl" as, could it be, happy. It earned a Best Pop Vocal Album nomination at the 2018 Grammys, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Radiohead and "Get Free": a dispute over echoes of "Creep"
years.p: A dispute over similarities between "Creep" and her song "Get Free" ended in summer 2017, according to Wikipedia.

q: This is the American dream, right now.
years.src: Wikipedia: Norman Fucking Rockwell! · Wikipedia: Lana Del Rey videography
years.h: Norman Fucking Rockwell!: Antonoff, a Sublime cover, 9.4 from Pitchfork
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 9.4; its Jenn Pelly called her one of America's greatest living songwriters. It debuted at No. 3 in the US and No. 1 in the UK.
years.xp:
Jack Antonoff produced it with Zach Dawes, Andrew Watt and Rick Nowels contributing. Metacritic scored it 87 and counted it the most-named album on 2019 year-end critic lists.

The Album of the Year nomination at the 62nd Grammys followed. Rolling Stone later placed it at No. 321 on its 500 Greatest Albums list. The title track's video was directed by her sister Chuck Grant.

eras.title: Two albums in seven months, and a stolen laptop
eras.text: She moves into books and a spoken-word release, then puts out two albums in 2021. A break-in in 2022 takes hard drives and a manuscript.

years.h: Violet Bent Backwards over the Grass, as an audiobook
years.p: Jack Antonoff produced the spoken-word recording. The physical poetry book followed on September 29.

years.src: Wikipedia: Chemtrails over the Country Club
years.h: Chemtrails over the Country Club closes on a Joni Mitchell cover
years.p: Weyes Blood and Zella Day join her on "For Free". It hit No. 1 in the UK, her fifth chart-topper there.
years.xp: Nikki Lane appears on "Breaking Up Slowly". Pitchfork scored it 7.5 and Metacritic 81, per Wikipedia. It was the UK's fastest-selling vinyl of the century for a female act.

years.h: Blue Banisters follows seven months later
years.p: It reached No. 8 in the US and No. 2 in the UK, with Zach Dawes, Drew Erickson and Rick Nowels among the producers.
years.xp: Pitchfork scored it 7.7. In a March 2023 Rolling Stone UK interview she said she made it as a response to accusations about cultural appropriation and glamorizing domestic abuse, per Wikipedia, and kept its promotion minimal.

years.h: A car break-in takes her laptop and a 200-page manuscript
years.p: The theft, per Wikipedia, also included hard drives, camcorders and unfinished songs. The manuscript was titled Behind the Iron Gates - Insights from an Institution.

years.h: "Snow on the Beach" with Taylor Swift
years.p: The Midnights track debuted at No. 4 on the Hot 100. A remix with an expanded Del Rey verse followed May 26, 2023.

eras.title: Ocean Blvd
eras.text: Her ninth album is recorded on voice memos, arrives two weeks late, and lands in critics' year-end lists with a Grammy Album of the Year nomination.

years.h: "A&W" arrives: two songs in one, recorded in two days
years.p: An acoustic first half gives way to a trap-flavored second half fans call "Jimmy".
years.xp: Antonoff has said the second part began as an outtake from the 2018 Norman Fucking Rockwell! sessions. Pitchfork's Shaad D'Souza named it Best New Track and called it a "psychedelic, collagist freakout". It was nominated for Song of the Year at the 66th Grammys.

years.cap: Did You Know That There's a Tunnel Under Ocean Blvd
years.src: Wikipedia: Did You Know That There's a Tunnel Under Ocean Blvd · Album of the Year: Lana Del Rey - Did you know
years.h: Ocean Blvd is Best New Music, then No. 11 on Pitchfork's 2023 list
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 8.3 and Best New Music, ranking it No. 11 of 2023. Its Olivia Horn called it a "sweeping, sterling, often confounding work".
years.xp:
She recorded raw vocal takes into her phone and sent them to Drew Erickson for orchestral arrangements. Mike Hermosa added piano, and Jack Antonoff arrived late. Guests include Jon Batiste, Father John Misty, SYML, Tommy Genesis and Bleachers, plus a sermon by Judah Smith. The title refers to the Jergins Tunnel in Long Beach, California, built in 1927 and closed in 1967.

The album was delayed from March 10 to March 24. It went to No. 1 in the UK and No. 3 in the US, with 41,000 and 115,000 units, per Wikipedia. Metacritic scores it 80. The Daily Telegraph's Neil McCormick called it boring, citing dull production and shapeless songs.

Photographer Neil Krug shot 65 candidate cover images. A nude photo she rejected for the standard cover was later used on limited vinyl editions.

years.h: She works a shift at a Waffle House in Florence, Alabama
years.p: She wore the employee uniform, per Wikipedia.

years.src: Wikipedia: Did You Know That There's a Tunnel Under Ocean Blvd · Wikipedia: Lana Del Rey
years.h: Five Grammy nominations, including Album of the Year
years.p: The Ocean Blvd album was also up for Best Alternative Music Album at the 66th Grammys.

eras.title: Stadiums and a country record
eras.text: She headlines Coachella and Fenway, records with Quavo and The Weeknd, and works on a country album whose title keeps changing.

years.cap: Lana Del Rey performing live at the Grammy Museum in Los Angeles on 10/13/2019. · Wikimedia
years.src: Consequence: Lana Del Rey Headlines Coachella · Wikipedia: Lana Del Rey
yt: Lana Del Rey and Billie Eilish, Video Games, Coachella 2024
years.h: First Coachella headline slot: Billie Eilish, Batiste and a hologram
years.p: Billie Eilish joined for "Ocean Eyes" and "Video Games" from a gilded balcony. Jon Batiste played keys while she pole-danced.
years.xp: She had first played Coachella in 2014. Antonoff played piano during the hologram number, per Consequence. Eilish said Del Rey "is the reason for half you bitches' existence - including mine"; the set ran 20 songs and revived rarities including a Sublime cover.

years.h: Fenway Park, her first solo stadium show, sells out
years.p: She announced it in April, the same month as Coachella.

years.h: "Tough" with Quavo previews her country album
years.p: She had announced the tenth album on January 31, 2024. Its title has changed from Lasso to The Right Person Will Stay to Stove.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists the title as Stove, confirmed in January 2026, with "Henry, Come On" and "Bluebird" released in spring 2025.

years.h: UK and Ireland stadium run: Wembley to Dublin, with Addison Rae opening
years.p: Six dates including Wembley, Cardiff, Glasgow, Liverpool and Dublin. London Grammar and Banks also opened.

years.h: "First Light" for the 007: First Light video game
years.p: She worked with composer David Arnold on the James Bond tie-in.
